specAnchors.text: CORE PRACTICAL 6 Chlorination of 2-methylpropan-2-ol with concentrated hydrochloric acid. Further suggested practicals: i the use of silver nitrate solution to identify the halogen present in halogenoalkanes ii preparation of 1-bromobutane from butan-1-ol, potassium bromide and sulfuric acid

primer.text: A tertiary alcohol needs no phosphorus reagent to become a chloride. This core practical shakes 2-methylpropan-2-ol with portioned concentrated hydrochloric acid, washes, dries and distils, collecting only the 47-53 degree fraction - with the fume hood doing non-negotiable duty throughout.

modules.title: Core Practical 6: making a tertiary chloride
sourceHeadings: Synthesis of a haloalkane from an alcohol
modules.opening: The tertiary alcohol route to a chloride needs no phosphorus reagent, just concentrated hydrochloric acid and patient shaking. This lesson walks the full synthesis, from portioned acid addition through washes and drying to the distillation window that isolates the product.
keyPoints: 8 cm3 of 2-methylpropan-2-ol is measured and poured into a separating funnel.
Concentrated hydrochloric acid, 20 cm3, is added in small 2-3 cm3 portions in a fume hood, venting after each addition.
The funnel stands for 20 minutes with gentle shaking at 2-minute intervals, then the lower aqueous layer is drained off.
Sodium hydrogencarbonate solution removes acidic impurities, and two spatulas of magnesium sulfate dry the organic layer.
The dry liquid is distilled and the fraction between 47 and 53 degrees collected as the product.

low.restatement: Add the acid in portions with venting, let the layers separate, wash with hydrogencarbonate, dry over magnesium sulfate, and distil, keeping only the fraction inside the 47-53 window.
low.analogy: Making a dressing: add the sharp ingredient gradually with venting, let the layers split, rinse, blot dry, then serve only the portion within the desired range.
low.examPointer: Quote each purification step with its purpose - hydrogencarbonate for acids, sulfate for water, distillation window for identity.

medium.restatement: The venting ritual exists because acid addition releases hydrogen chloride gas pressure, and the hydrogencarbonate wash releases carbon dioxide as it neutralises; the distillation window brackets the product's boiling point so impurities boiling outside it are excluded.
medium.analogy: A kettle vented as it fills: pressure that is not released builds until it spits; each portion addition is a fill-and-vent cycle.
medium.examPointer: Explain why the fume hood is mandatory - concentrated acid releases toxic hydrogen chloride the moment its container is uncovered.

glossary.definition: A sodium hydrogencarbonate wash that neutralises and removes acidic impurities from an organic layer.
The narrow distillation temperature bracket, here 47-53 degrees, within which the pure product is collected.
An extracted, enclosed workspace that draws toxic or irritant vapours away from the chemist at their source.
The water-rich layer in a separating funnel, drained off to leave the organic product behind.
